topic: Can satellite orbital configurations optimize ML-based QoS by reducing propagation delays for latency-sensitive traffic classes?
consensus_response: Satellite orbital configurations can optimize Machine Learning (ML)-based Quality of Service (QoS) by reducing propagation delays for latency-sensitive traffic classes. Geo-synchronous orbits (GSO) offer minimal latency, but require more satellites for global coverage, increasing initial deployment costs. Lower orbits like Medium Earth Orbit (MEO)/Low Earth Orbit (LEO) provide faster data rates but higher latency due to increased signal propagation times. Advanced modulation techniques like M-QAM and OTFS can further reduce latency by improving spectral efficiency. However, these techniques increase design complexity and power consumption. A path selection mechanism that considers satellite link characteristics, including high fixed latencies, is required for optimal performance in converged networks with parallel links.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the challenges of providing Quality of Service (QoS) guarantees in converged satellite and terrestrial networks, particularly due to high fixed latencies associated with satellite links. Current QoS mechanisms focus on managing available capacity but do not consider these latency impacts when choosing paths for certain traffic.
